messages.content: I bought the Sunday 2:25 Delta flight after we spoke, so leave that alone. I need to settle the three hotel nights and the Wednesday return now. Please compare the hotel totals, not just the nightly rates, and tell me what the morning trip to the Baltimore Museum of Art would actually be like.

I found three refundable options for Sunday, August 16 through Wednesday, August 19. The Inn at The Colonnade is $744.63 total: $639.00 room charge and $105.63 tax, with no destination fee. It is about a 10-minute walk to the museum's main entrance. Hotel Revival in Mount Vernon is $622.39 total: $537.00 room charge and $85.39 tax, also with no destination fee. A weekday rideshare to the museum is generally 8 to 12 minutes around 7:00 a.m., but I would allow 20 minutes door to door. The Hampton Inn & Suites Baltimore Inner Harbor is $548.76 total: $471.00 room charge and $77.76 tax. Its morning rideshare is normally 15 to 22 minutes and can reach 30 minutes in heavier traffic. None of those totals includes parking, which you do not need for this trip.
Is breakfast included at any of them, and are those routes realistic for a 7:30 start Monday? I do not want the cheapest room if it creates a shaky commute.

The Hampton includes breakfast. The Colonnade and Revival rates do not. For a 7:30 a.m. museum start, the Colonnade is the simplest: leave around 7:10 and walk. From Revival, requesting a car by 6:55 should normally put you at the museum between 7:10 and 7:20. From the Hampton, I would request one by 6:40 because the route uses downtown streets and the Jones Falls Expressway. All three are workable, but the Hampton has the most variable trip despite its lower total.
What is the cancellation deadline for Revival, and is there any fee that only appears at checkout? Also check whether the room is a real king, not a request.

The available Revival rate confirms one king bed. The $622.39 is the complete lodging charge for all three nights, including the 15.9% combined hotel taxes. There is no resort or destination fee. Incidentals and optional services would be separate. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. Baltimore time on Friday, August 14; after that, the penalty is the first night's room and tax, $195.87.

Revival sounds like the right balance. Before booking it, look at the Wednesday flight terms. The carrier may release us Tuesday afternoon. I need to be able to abandon Wednesday and take the Tuesday 8:35 without losing the Wednesday fare.

The Wednesday Delta nonstop at 9:05 a.m. has two relevant one-way fares. Standard Main Cabin is $139.00 and has no change fee, but canceling it would leave the value as a Delta eCredit. Main Cabin Refundable is $218.00 and can be canceled before departure for a refund to the original payment method. Since the Tuesday 8:35 p.m. fallback is on Southwest, the refundable Delta fare is the one that lets you cancel Wednesday without trapping that money in a Delta credit. You would still need to buy the Southwest ticket at its price available then.
Could I change the refundable Delta ticket to a Tuesday Delta flight instead if one works?

Yes. Delta allows the refundable ticket to be changed before departure without a change fee. You would pay any higher fare, or receive the difference back to the original payment method if the replacement refundable fare is lower. Delta currently has Tuesday nonstops at 4:20 p.m. and 7:15 p.m. The 4:20 is probably too early for the uncertain handoff; the 7:15 is $246.00 in refundable Main Cabin, so moving to it at today's prices would add $28.00.
The 7:15 might still be tight. Keep Southwest 8:35 as the practical fallback. What time would I have to leave Revival for the Wednesday 9:05 Delta flight?

For the Wednesday departure, I would leave Revival at 6:35 a.m. The drive to BWI is commonly 20 to 30 minutes at that hour, and allowing up to 40 minutes puts you at the terminal around 7:15. That leaves about 90 minutes before departure for security and the walk to the gate. The hotel can arrange a car, or you can request a rideshare that morning.
All right. Book Revival for the three nights and the $218 refundable Wednesday return. Do not make any change to the Sunday ticket.

Before I submit both, the charges will be $622.39 for Hotel Revival and $218.00 for the Delta refundable one-way ticket, for $840.39 charged now. The hotel is Sunday through Tuesday nights with Wednesday checkout, and the flight is BWI to ATL Wednesday, August 19, departing 9:05 a.m. and arriving 11:02 a.m. The existing Sunday outbound will remain untouched. Shall I complete those purchases?
Yes, complete them.

Both purchases are confirmed. Hotel Revival confirmation RVB-81642 is for one king room, check-in Sunday, August 16 and checkout Wednesday, August 19. The complete hotel charge is $622.39, and cancellation remains free through 6:00 p.m. local time Friday, August 14. Delta confirmation G4N7TX is for the refundable Main Cabin nonstop from BWI to ATL on Wednesday at 9:05 a.m., arriving 11:02 a.m., charged at $218.00. Your Sunday reservation was not modified.
Does the Delta confirmation clearly say refundable to the card, rather than just changeable?

Yes. The receipt identifies the fare as Main Cabin Refundable and states that cancellation before departure returns the ticket value to the original form of payment. Changes before departure have no change fee, though a fare difference can apply. After departure or a no-show, the refund right is not preserved, so the Wednesday segment must be canceled before its scheduled departure if you switch to Tuesday.
Good. If the release is confirmed Tuesday morning and I choose Southwest, what exactly needs to happen?

First purchase the Tuesday 8:35 p.m. Southwest nonstop while the acceptable fare is available. Then cancel Delta confirmation G4N7TX before Wednesday's departure and verify that the $218.00 refund is going to the original card. Hotel Revival can be shortened to a Tuesday checkout only if its rate desk permits the change; the current reservation guarantees all three nights, and dropping Tuesday night after the August 14 deadline could still leave that night chargeable.
Can the hotel tell us now whether shortening it would be allowed?

The hotel's reservation desk says a shortened stay made before 6:00 p.m. August 14 can be repriced without penalty, subject to the two-night rate then available. After that deadline, an early departure may incur up to one night's room and tax. They cannot waive that prospectively because it depends on occupancy. Keeping Tuesday night would let you work through the handoff, collect your bag, and leave for BWI without checking out in the morning.

Then keep all three nights even if I fly Tuesday. It is worth having the room through the workday. Give me the full expected trip total, including the Sunday flight I already bought and a reasonable transportation allowance.

Using the $113.00 already paid for Sunday's Delta outbound, $622.39 for Hotel Revival, $218.00 for Wednesday's refundable return, and a $90.00 allowance for rideshares between BWI, the hotel, and the museum, the expected total is $1,043.39. If you switch to Southwest Tuesday, replace the $218.00 return cost with the Southwest fare after the Delta refund; the three-night hotel charge stays $622.39.
That is clear. Final status, including the fallback, please.

Confirmed: Delta ATL-BWI on Sunday, August 16 at 2:25 p.m.; Hotel Revival king room for Sunday through Tuesday nights at a complete $622.39; and refundable Delta BWI-ATL on Wednesday, August 19 at 9:05 a.m. for $218.00. Leave Revival around 6:35 a.m. Wednesday. The expected trip total is $1,043.39 including a $90.00 transportation allowance. If Tuesday release is confirmed, the 8:35 p.m. Southwest nonstop remains the practical fallback: buy it first, then cancel the Wednesday Delta segment before departure for a refund to the original card. Keep the Tuesday hotel night in either case.
